titleDv: ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޤާނޫނުއަސާސީއަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This government bill amends the Constitution of the Maldives. It says any change to the Maldives' sea areas, including the exclusive economic zone, or anything that reduces them, needs a law passed by at least two-thirds of all MPs. It makes MPs lose their seat if they leave, are expelled from, or switch the party they were elected for, or if an independent MP joins a party. It also requires a majority of all MPs to approve any foreign military use of Maldivian territory or foreign troops operating there, and adds long-term national development planning to the President's duties.
whyItMatters: Parliament, not the government alone, would have to approve border or sea-area changes and foreign military activity in the Maldives, and MPs who switch parties mid-term would lose their seats.
keyProvisions: Article 3 is split into two parts. New 3(b) says the internal waters, archipelagic waters, territorial sea, contiguous zone and exclusive economic zone can only be changed or reduced by a law passed by at least two-thirds of all MPs.

A new Article 73(e), after 73(d), says an MP loses their seat if, during the term they were elected for, they leave or are expelled from the party they represent or join another party. An MP elected as an independent loses their seat on joining a political party.
Article 115(e) adds a duty for the President to set short, medium and long-term national development plans and visions, alongside setting the state's main policies.

Article 251(c) is rewritten so no foreign power may use any part of Maldivian territory for military purposes, by agreement or otherwise, without approval by a majority of all MPs. Foreign troops may not operate in the Maldives for military purposes without that approval, except when taking part in exercises held under an agreement.
Adds a fourth item to Article 262(c) that refers to Article 262(c) itself, under a heading about the President assenting to bills. The text does not make clear what practical effect this has.
The changes take effect once passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette (clause 6).
whoIsAffected: Members of Parliament and political parties, the President and government, and any foreign country seeking military access to the Maldives.
statedReasons: The government says the bill makes changes to Maldivian sea areas require a two-thirds law, makes foreign military use of Maldivian territory require Parliament's approval, and makes MPs lose their seat if the status they were elected under changes.
